primary_estimand: Effect of hindlimb unloading (disuse; 1, 3, 7 days) and subsequent reloading/recovery (free cage activity 1, 3, 7 days after 7-day unloading) versus active cage controls on TSS-peak / gene expression, separately in soleus and EDL (S2.2.p1, S2.7.8.p1)
sample_inclusion: 21 Wistar rats, 3 per group, both muscles per rat (S2.1.p1, S2.2.p1)
planned_contrasts: each phase (D1, D3, D7, R1, R3, R7) vs control, per muscle (S2.7.8.p1, FIG3; counts only in Figure 3A / ST4, not in text)
time-course comparisons between consecutive phases (S3.3.p1, ST4C,D)
repeated_measure_unit: rat (soleus and EDL from the same animal); muscles analysed separately
paper_method: DESeq2 on CAGE TSS peaks, peak-level; gene DE if any peak in gene is DE (S2.7.8.p1)
paper_results: DEG counts per phase only in Figure 3A (not stated numerically in text); R1 soleus has the most DEGs (S3.3.p2)
exercise_arm: none: no exercise training or acute exercise bout; 'recovery' is release from tail suspension into normal cage activity (S2.2.p1)
